title: Coding Arena
subtitle: Multiplayer Coding Competition Platform
keyFeatures: Real-time multiplayer platform where developers compete through coding, debugging, DSA, SQL, logic, output-prediction and programming puzzles
Supports 1v1, Free-for-All and Team-based matches with private rooms for up to 10 players
Custom game rooms with configurable categories, difficulty, rounds, duration and team settings
Real-time match synchronization using Socket.IO for player states, timers, submissions, scores and match events
Interactive coding challenges powered by Monaco Editor, alongside non-coding challenge formats such as MCQs, output prediction and debugging
Ranked progression system with MMR/rating, leagues, streaks, achievements and seasonal leaderboards
Friend system supporting friend requests, online status, challenges, room invitations and match history
results: Built the platform around a reusable question engine, allowing new challenges to be introduced without changing frontend or backend game logic
Designed a real-time multiplayer architecture capable of synchronizing players, timers, submissions and scores across an active match
Created a progression system that connects performance → rating → league → difficulty, giving players a reason to continue playing
Designed multiple challenge formats so the platform is not limited to traditional competitive programming
Established a scalable foundation for future features such as spectator mode, tournaments, seasonal rankings, category-specific ratings and additional game modes
challenges: Designing a real-time state-management system where all players must see consistent timers, scores and match states
Preventing race conditions when multiple players submit answers or disconnect at the same time
Designing a flexible question schema capable of supporting completely different challenge types such as MCQ, debugging, output prediction, SQL and full coding problems
Building matchmaking and rating logic that remains fair across different skill levels, game modes and player counts
Handling multiplayer room lifecycle including creation, joining, leaving, reconnecting, ready states and match completion
lessonsLearned: Real-time multiplayer applications require a different architecture from conventional CRUD applications because state synchronization becomes a core problem
Game logic should be separated from question data so the platform can scale from dozens to thousands of challenges without rewriting application logic
WebSockets are useful for transient multiplayer state, while MongoDB is better suited for persistent entities such as users, matches, ratings, questions and achievements
Competitive progression works better when rating/MMR is separated from individual match scores

title: Last Stand
subtitle: Real-time multiplayer social strategy game
keyFeatures: A real-time multiplayer platform targeting 20–50 concurrent players, with React and three.js clients talking to a Node.js/TypeScript backend over WebSockets
Server-authoritative gameplay: clients send player intents, the backend validates actions and applies state transitions, then synchronises updated state back to every connected client
Island — the flagship multiplayer experience — built around cooperative tasks, hidden roles, fragmented information, real-time communication and constrained voting
Tournament progression that carries player state across matches and narrows the player pool round by round toward a two-player final
architectureNotes: Reusable multiplayer services for matchmaking, private rooms, real-time lobbies, persistent sessions, and reconnect/recovery — shared infrastructure multiple games can sit on top of
Versioned, schema-first message contracts shared between the TypeScript and three.js clients, with generated types to keep the web client, backend and 3D client in sync

Application data split into static game content, dynamic match state, and persistent player data — in-memory real-time state kept separate from PostgreSQL-backed accounts, match history, progression and telemetry
whatsNext: Finishing the standalone AI game mode, so the core gameplay loop is playable against AI-controlled opponents outside of live matches
Rounding out the tournament bracket flow and match lifecycle management
This is an active project — the multiplayer foundation, lobby/session layer and Island prototype are underway, not the full game

title: Portfolio Website
subtitle: City-themed interactive developer portfolio
keyFeatures: Interactive portfolio with a city-skyline metaphor where projects are presented as buildings in a dynamic day/night theme
Smooth animations and scroll-triggered reveals using Framer Motion for engaging narrative flow
Fully responsive design that adapts seamlessly from mobile (390px) to desktop (1920px) with a hamburger menu and touch-friendly interactions
Accessible component system with high contrast ratios (AA/AAA WCAG compliance) across light and dark modes
Rich project cards with live demos, GitHub links, tech stacks, architecture diagrams and detailed feature/results/challenges content
results: Created a memorable, interactive first impression that stands out from traditional portfolio formats
Built a modular design system in Tailwind that scales across all breakpoints while maintaining visual consistency
Achieved pixel-perfect animations and micro-interactions that enhance the user experience without compromising performance
Implemented a theme-aware token system that ensures correct contrast in both light and dark modes
challenges: Designing a metaphor (city skyline) that communicates portfolio information intuitively while remaining visually engaging
Ensuring smooth animations across all breakpoints without performance degradation on mobile devices
Managing a complex token system to enforce consistent, accessible color usage across components
Building responsive layouts that work seamlessly from 390px mobile width to 1920px+ desktop displays
lessonsLearned: A strong visual metaphor makes a portfolio memorable and differentiates it from competitors
Investing in a design token system early made it possible to ensure accessibility across themes
Mobile-first responsive design is essential — desktop can look great, but mobile forces you to prioritize clarity
Animations should enhance, not distract — purposeful motion adds delight without sacrificing usability

title: InsightPDF
subtitle: Agentic RAG document intelligence platform
keyFeatures: Agentic document intelligence platform that ingests large document collections and uses stateful LangGraph workflows to retrieve, extract, analyse, compare and generate evidence-backed results beyond conventional RAG Q&A

Document capability system that classifies uploads by type and exposes task-specific workflows for research papers, literature and study material, alongside universal summarisation and conversational Q&A
Interactive learning workflows that generate chapter summaries, notes, quizzes, flashcards and configurable question papers, grounded in the uploaded material
Book/literature workflows with spoiler-controlled summaries, chapter analysis, character and theme analysis, and contextual Q&A with user-controlled detail and spoiler levels
results: An agentic tool layer for semantic retrieval, section/page lookup, structured extraction, document comparison, calculation and report generation, with workflows selecting tools based on user intent
Iterative retrieval and validation that evaluates evidence, refines queries when needed, and grounds every response with document- and page-level citations
A model-agnostic LLM gateway using cloud APIs as the primary reasoning layer with automatic fallback to local Ollama models when quotas or availability run out
An evaluation and observability layer measuring retrieval relevance, answer faithfulness, citation accuracy, latency and agent/tool execution
challenges: Keeping multi-step agentic workflows grounded — evaluating evidence and refining retrieval instead of letting the model answer from prior knowledge
Separating deterministic processing (parsing, calculation, retrieval, validation) from agentic planning so workflow behaviour stays controllable
Designing task-specific workflows (study material vs. literature vs. research papers) without duplicating the retrieval/citation core
lessonsLearned: A model-agnostic gateway with local fallback removed a single point of failure without adding much complexity
Investing in an evaluation layer early made it possible to actually measure whether agentic changes were improvements
Document-type-aware capabilities were more useful to build than one generic Q&A workflow

title: Seismic Event Detection System
subtitle: CNN + Transformer pipeline for earthquake detection & risk alerts
keyFeatures: Deep learning system combining CNN and Transformer architectures for earthquake detection, magnitude estimation and epicenter location prediction
Power Spectral Density (PSD) features integrated for enhanced frequency-domain analysis
Multi-stage pipeline over STEAD seismic waveform data for event classification, geolocation and risk-based alerting
Interactive dashboard for seismic monitoring and prediction analysis
results: Improved magnitude prediction accuracy through PSD-based frequency features
End-to-end pipeline covering detection, classification, geolocation and alerting
challenges: Extracting reliable frequency-domain signal from noisy real-world waveform data
Combining CNN and Transformer representations without losing localization precision
lessonsLearned: Frequency-domain features (PSD) added real signal beyond raw waveform inputs
Visualization and evaluation tooling were as important as the model itself for a monitoring use case

title: Traffic Signal Management
subtitle: Multi-agent reinforcement learning for adaptive traffic control
keyFeatures: PPO-based RL model that optimizes traffic signal timings using SUMO-simulated real-world traffic data
Custom reward strategies that prioritize high-traffic lanes to reduce overall urban congestion
results: Adaptive signal timing that responds to simulated real-time traffic load
Reward shaping tuned specifically toward congestion reduction on high-traffic lanes
challenges: Designing a reward function that balances fairness across lanes with overall throughput
Getting stable multi-agent training convergence in a shared traffic environment
lessonsLearned: Reward shaping mattered more than raw model capacity for this environment
SUMO simulation fidelity was key to getting policies that would generalize

title: ArcFlow
subtitle: AI-driven branching narrative platform
keyFeatures: AI-driven story platform with dynamic branching choices
Genre/mood-aware generative API integration for narrative progression
Secure per-user story history management
results: Fully dynamic branching narratives generated on the fly rather than pre-scripted
Persistent, isolated story history per user
challenges: Keeping generated narrative continuity coherent across branching choices
Designing a data model that supports per-user branching story state
lessonsLearned: Mood/genre conditioning noticeably improved narrative consistency
Clean separation between story-state storage and generation logic simplified branching
